summary: L-4 groundhouse on Little Snowy Top in Idaho's Priest Lake country; restored by volunteers in the 1980s and burned to the ground on September 3, 2016.

facts.status_note: Burned to the ground on September 3, 2016. No source we read describes what, if anything, remains.

access.note: Reached by a nine-mile trail on foot or horse. No closure is reported in our sources, and none describes the site today.

visit.trail_note: Nine miles on foot or by horse; the cabin burned to the ground in 2016, so there is no structure to climb.

events.note: Register gives circa 1930 to 1933; Spokesman-Review says built between 1930 and 1933. The record's 1930 is the start of that range.
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Howard Thomason as known staff for 1933. Fan-site list, not checked against a primary source.
A grizzly bear broke in and chased the lookout staffer into the rafters, per the Spokesman-Review.
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Rupert Cutler as known staff for 1952. Fan-site list, not checked against a primary source.
Weebly quotes an October 1983 item about a 'Little Snowy Lookout Tower' donated to Priest River in 1982; the item does not clearly say whether it is this cabin.
Register dates volunteer work to 1987 as a two-year effort; a 1989 item quoted on the Weebly page says the project began in 1987. The Spokesman-Review says restoration started in 1988.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register.
During the Hughes fires the lookout was covered with retardant and a fire-resistant wrap.
Burned to the ground on September 3, 2016, in the afternoon. Spokesman-Review says it likely burned due to carelessness with the wood stove; Weebly gives the same cause more broadly.
The register says the tower was destroyed in a September 3, 2016 fire.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register.

notes_for_editor: Core history agrees across sources: built about 1930 to 1933, decommissioned in the 1960s, restored by volunteers, burned 3 Sept 2016. Open points: (1) restoration start is 1987 in the register and the 1989 item but 1988 in the Spokesman-Review; (2) elevation is 6,590 ft (2,009 m) in the register, matching the record's 2008.6 m, but 6829 ft on firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com; (3) a 1983 Weebly item about a 'Little Snowy Lookout Tower' donated to Priest River may or may not concern this cabin; (4) the 'public' access level is inferred from the trail and the lack of any closure notice, not from a current access statement; (5) staff names come only from a fan site. The record's status and kind look correct; no correction proposed. The register calls the 2016 structure a tower in one line, which we treat as a register wording issue.
